issues.description: Method return-type mismatch for SealSaloon.checkOrderReady(): The problem statement UML declares checkOrderReady() with return type void (problem_statement.md line 32), but the reference solution defines it as public boolean checkOrderReady() (solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java line 20). This inconsistency can confuse students about the expected signature and may cause grader/tests or student implementations to disagree about whether the method should return a boolean status or be void.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent between spec and implementation. Either (A) change the solution method signature to 'public void checkOrderReady()' and remove the boolean return value (preserving the same internal behavior but using no return), or (B) update the problem statement UML and textual description to declare 'checkOrderReady(): boolean' and explain the meaning of the boolean return. Prefer option (A) to match the existing UML/spec and avoid requiring students to return a value.
